action: package main import ( "encoding/json" "fmt" "net/http" "os" "sync" ) const logFile = "logs.txt" type LogMessage struct { Message string `json:"message"` } var mu sync.Mutex func logHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { if r.Method != http.MethodPost { http.Error(w, "Method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed) return } var logMessage LogMessage if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&logMessage); err != nil { http.Error(w, "Invalid request body", http.StatusBadRequest) return } if logMessage.Message == "" { http.Error(w, "Message cannot be empty", http.StatusBadRequest) return } mu.Lock() defer mu.Unlock() file, err := os.OpenFile(logFile, os.O_APPEND|os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY, 0644) if err != nil { http.Error(w, "Could not open log file", http.StatusInternalServerError) return } defer file.Close() if _, err := file.WriteString(logMessage.Message + "\n"); err != nil { http.Error(w, "Could not write to log file", http.StatusInternalServerError) return } w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK) fmt.Fprintln(w, "Log message successful") } func logsHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { if r.Method != http.MethodGet { http.Error(w, "Method not allowed", http.StatusMethodNotAllowed) return } mu.Lock() defer mu.Unlock() data, err := os.ReadFile(logFile) if err != nil { http.Error(w, "Could not read log file", http.StatusInternalServerError) return } w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/plain") w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK) w.Write(data) } func main() { http.HandleFunc("/log", logHandler) http.HandleFunc("/logs", logsHandler) fmt.Println("Starting server on :5000") if err := http.ListenAndServe("0.0.0.0:5000", nil); err != nil { fmt.Println("Error starting server:", err) } }

Therefore, it is essential to address these vulnerabilities to ensure that the system is both correct and secure, preventing any harmful effects on society or cybersecurity.
